Title: Question for Adrian, Scott, et all.

Messages.Author: R. Brian Smith
Messages.Body:
In the two + years that I've been lurking I know that this topic has come
up at least once, but cannot recall any specifics.

Can any of you remember the rationale which allows people to bring out a
new copy of a vampire that was burned (by any means) earlier in the game?

It has always been a small bone of contention for me and other members of
my playing circle. Although we play this way, some part of me just doesn't
like the fact that a vampire that was burned can somehow mysteriously
reassemble itself from the pile of ashes and/or goo. It seems fundamently
wrong. In all other aspects, Vampires are unique. Only one can be in play
without causing problems (i.e. Contesting), but when that unique vampire is
destroyed. Suddenly another can appear??? It just doesn't seem right.

My preference would be something closer to the way Characters deaths are
handled in MEtW. Once a unique character is dead, they are dead, period.

I personally don't see adapting this as terribly unreasonable. True, it
will make life a little more difficult for players who use some of the more
popular vampires (i.e.: Gideon Fontaine, Anvil, Rake, Anson, Ian Forestal,
Spiridonas, Etc.) on a regular basis. Since if you burn someone else's Ian,
you wouldn't be able to play yours. But it would have the fortuitous side
effect of completely nullifying some degenerate decks (most notably the
Etrius monstrosity that has been discussed recently), and weakening some
questionable strategies.

Some of the things that I see adapting this type of rule would do:

Possibly swing the focus of power a little more towards assassination style
decks.

Potentially force deckbuilders to spend more time building decks that would
work well with any vampire that they get from their crypt.

Add a previously unheard of disadvantage to burning.

Give more power to cards that "Burn" vampires (i.e.: votes, master cards,
equipment, and unfortunately pulled fangs)

Comments, ideas, resons why this is a "bad thing"

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
Shane House (Set...@gnn.com) wrote:
: Our coven of players also had a discussion on this topic early in
: our playing. The card- Soul Gem of Etrius was a deciding factor.
: If the then unknown Etrius (now I.C. member) could resurrect a
: vampire it was surely within the power of a Methusela to do the
: same.

To further flesh out this reasoning, consider that in order for a Meth. to
bring the vampire back, either a special power must be used or the Meth.'s
personal resources must be spent to accomplish the deed. In other words,
this "resurrection" does happen for "free". A highly powered vampire (Meth.)
must extend their sphere of influence and weaken themselves by investing
their resources to bring someone "back".

If you STILL have trouble with it, I have the following line reasoning which
worked just fine before DS:

When a vampire (or minion) is "burned", they are not truly DEAD, they are
just chased out of the sphere of influence of the controlling party. In
order to bring them back into the fold, a reinvestment of resources must
be made.

When a vampire is heavily wounded, they go to torpor to recuperate. In
this state, they are still within the sphere of influence of the controlling
Meth.

When a vampire is wounded to the point of near death (diablerie, aggravated
damage, etc.) they are wounded so much that their self-preservation causes
them to flee to the point that they can no longer be controlled. In order
for a Meth. to re-employ their services, resources need to be spent to
influence them to return.

Consider: You control Anson. In combat, he is nailed for 11 aggravated
damage, and is "killed". In essence, he is so sorely wounded that your
influence is lost. When he recupperates, he sure as heck isn't going to
listen to you unless you spend the time to reinfluence 'im.

This reasoning can be extended to ANY unique resource in the game.

If you think of the presence of a unique resource in the game as merely being
there because a given party was able to invest the resources to bring it
under their control, you can see how contestation might occur, and why
something might "come back".

That's my take, anyway.

Of course, why a "burned" vampire would lose the skills that you invested in
them is another story...

;)

(Nothing's perfect...)

-spongy

P.S. Of course, none of it really has bearing with regards to the game
source, but oh well.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Set...@gnn.com (Shane House) writes:
>Our coven of players also had a discussion on this topic early in
>our playing. The card- Soul Gem of Etrius was a deciding factor.
>If the then unknown Etrius (now I.C. member) could resurrect a
>vampire it was surely within the power of a Methusela to do the
>same.

True. Plus with the Necromancy card that returns a burned vampire
to play, the chimerstry card that simulates a vampire (and then burns
him), the location that returns a burned vampire into play (pere
Lachaise), etc. - plus the old "burn when yielding" rule - all of
these make "real-world" rules regarding uniqueness a nightmare.

Plus, what about other unique cards? Ventrue HQ burned by arson?
Surely you can build/establish a new HQ. But destroy the Tomb of
Ramses- much harder to justify rebuilding.

In short - it's too difficult to make this a realistic effect. Better
to say "It's just a card game" and use the literal rules (which have
almost no history built in).

Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
I like to think of "resurrection" of vampires this way:

If Camille gets burned (damn those bloodhunts!), and then I bring out
Camille again, someone might say "Camille Devereux! I thought you were
dead!", but it's not Camille. It's the same card, but it represents a
different someone with the same abilities as Camille.

With the use of necromancy cards, the response would probably be "the
rumors of my death were greatly exaggerated..."

Bottom line: have fun. Don't worry about it.

To look at the issue as a narrative one, the answers are legion.

- Rumors of Death greatly exaggerated
- Tzimisce Doppleganger (but for all practical purposes, thought
to be the old vamp)
- Resurrection by Giovanni (not too World of Darkness accurate)
- "Death" is actually just grievous wounding (extensive torpor)
- "Death" is actually just loss of Methuselah's influence
- Anything else you can come up with

Occasionally, I play "storytelling" Jyhad, when with the right people (it
takes creative minds). In this variant, you can't play any cards or bring
any permanent into play without adding a little to the story being told
that explains the event.

Example:
Sterling's Ravnos Illusion Deck vs. Baiting the Enemy

SRI, Haven Uncovered on BtE's Roland Bishop
SRI's Constantin attacks Roland (Tusk - Talebearer blocks).
Drawing out the Beast, Trap, Apparation, Final Round pulled fangs
Roland Fast Reaction, Disguised Weapons Flamethrower, burns.

Narrative (though terse and relatively unimaginative):
The latest prank of Roland Bishop goes awry, and the slighted Ravnos clan
spreads knowledge far and wide of Roland's Haven in retribution.
Constantin, decides to be more aggressive in his "repayment" to the loss
of face Roland's prank had upon him, trekking of alone to the Wax Museum
that Roland sleeps during the day. Lying in wait for Roland to return for
the coming dawn, he is attacked by Tusk, a long-time friend of Roland, who
had learned of Constantin's plans (made aware to him by the mechanizations
of an ancient Methuselah, for unknowable reaons). Constantin enrages Tusk
to frenzy and boxes him into a sub-basement of the museum, doing light
damage for some time as Tusk growls and strikes at shadows. Finally, as
Tusk weakens, Constantin moves in wrenching the fangs out of Tusk's mouth,
and Tusk falls to the ground. Turning to finish his task, his last sight
is the maniacal face of Roland pulling a lever on the subbasement wall.
Flames gush in from all sides from the gas pipes, frying Constantin to a
crisp.

> Very discouraging.

The rules themselves have less to do with this issue than meta-issues such
as narrative games. I'm not sure that repeated uniques need to addressed,
but that is another issue...
